AUTHOR: Shah
TITLE: A Zero Shot Detection Based Approach for Fish Species Recognition in Underwater Environments
REGION: Gulf of Mexico, USA (NOAA SEFSC video surveys)
SPECIES: 51 reef fish classes selected from SEAMAPD21 (44 seen / 7 unseen: Lutjanus campechanus, Pagrus pagrus, Rhomboplites aurorubens, Seriola dumerili, Pristipomoides aquilonaris, Epinephelus morio, Holacanthus bermudensis)
DATA: SEAMAPD21 public dataset (130 classes, 28,319 images; 51 classes used)
D2: Seen/unseen class split 44/7; image-level train/test partition not described
D_EV: no statement found (Sec. III-B: 'we use the seen/unseen split of 44/7' refers to classes, not to an image/video partition)
R_EV: Sec. III-B: 'The dataset used in this study is the Southeast Area Monitoring and Assessment Program Dataset 2021 (SEAMAPD21)' — single dataset; unseen classes come from the same data
C_EV: no statement found (Table I varies the IoU threshold 0.4–0.7, not a confidence threshold)
E_EV: Sec. III-B: 'We utilize the mean average precision (mAP) as our evaluation metric' — only mAP/AP reported
ARCH: ZSD-FR: Faster R-CNN (ResNet-101) backbone trained on seen classes + conditional WGAN feature synthesizer with triplet, mode-seeking and cyclic-consistency losses; 300-d FastText class embeddings
METR: mAP at IoU 0.4/0.5/0.6/0.7 for seen and unseen classes; per-class AP; t-SNE of generated features
NOTE: Zero-shot detection on SEAMAPD21; unseen classes are not treated as an external test (same dataset/cameras), so R1 = N. Train/test image partition is never described (D1 = NR); SEAMAPD21 has a predefined image-level split but the paper does not say it was used. Platform not stated in text (SEAMAP surveys are known to use stationary camera arrays; verifier may set PLAT = 고정 카메라/관측소). 'Reef fish' in the Gulf of Mexico (hard-bottom reefs); ENV = 산호초 is the closest allowed value. Backbone pretraining (ImageNet/COCO) not stated. NIMG is the full SEAMAPD21 size; the 51-class subset size is not reported.
